How to play

  • Two action points a turn, on a turn timer. Blue tiles cost 1 AP, yellow dash tiles cost 2. Tap a tile to preview cover, tap again to move.
  • Full cover blocks 40 aim, half cover 20. Shots inside the graze band deal half damage instead of missing outright.
  • High ground (raised platforms and rooftops) gives +15 aim and +2 sight (+3 on a two-story roof). From above, half cover gives no protection and full cover only counts as half. Climbing onto a platform costs 1 extra move.
  • Many buildings, bunkers, temples, mesas, containers, huts, souk houses, rock shelves, stilt houses, lab blocks, crags, pagodas, parked trains, control towers and tenements have walkable rooftops, some with a second story. Climb the yellow ladders: +1 move per level climbed or descended. On the ground, walls and buildings block sight; from a rooftop you see and shoot over anything lower than you, except someone hugging the far side of a wall or building as tall as your roof. Grenades don’t reach from a rooftop down to the street, or up.
  • A platform or building edge right next to you is full cover against attackers below its top, but none against anyone standing on it or higher. Rooftops themselves give no cover: you trade protection for aim and sight.
  • Buildings with interiors have doors and windows. Windows are half cover you can see through. A closed door is full cover and blocks sight; walking through one opens it (+1 move). Next to a door you can open or close it (free, once a turn) or Breach it (1 AP: smashes it and stuns enemies right behind it).
  • Cover breaks. A missed shot at someone behind crates, cars, fences, windows or sandbags hits the cover instead (half the weapon’s minimum damage), and you can shoot objects directly (never misses, 1 ammo). At 0 HP full cover drops to half cover and half cover to rubble. Grenades knock everything in the blast down a stage.
  • Terrain: shallow water (Mirefen Marsh, the quarry sump, the Drowned Quarter streets, a flooded tunnel, hot springs) costs 1 extra move to wade into; boardwalks, pavements and bridges are dry. Lava (Cinder Lab), the monastery gorge and the deep canal cannot be crossed, only bridged, but block no sight or shots. Shooting a junction box (Drowned Quarter, Underline Transit) electrifies the water around it.
  • Geysers (Frostvent Caldera): from round 2 each vent erupts every 3 rounds at the start of the round, throwing up a steam cloud that blocks sight like smoke through the next round and scalding anyone standing on it for 2 damage. A vent about to erupt glows and pulses a round ahead.
  • Fuel barrels, oil drums, fuel and coolant tanks and blasting charges explode when destroyed, hurting everyone nearby and setting off other explosives in the blast. Shoot them when an enemy hides next to one.
  • Return fire: an operative in full cover from its attacker shoots back once per enemy turn (reaction shot, −15 aim, 1 ammo) if it survives, can see the shooter and has ammo. Not while downed, disoriented, hunkered or on overwatch. Flank to avoid it.
  • Information: gunfire and explosions out of sight within 14 tiles of your team show as ripples, edge arrows and minimap pings, and enemies leave a “?” marker where you last saw, heard or sensed them, fading over 2 rounds. The Scout Drone reveals an area until the end of next round; the Motion Sensor pings enemies that move near it for 4 rounds.
  • Grenades and other throwables cost 1 AP. Shooting or throwing a grenade before you move leaves 1 AP for a move; attacking after a move, overwatch and hunker end your turn. The railgun and gauss rifle need both AP.
  • Every weapon has an optimal range where its aim is best.
  • Every operative carries a secondary. Knives, axes and blades strike an adjacent enemy (the machete and Monoblade dash a few tiles to reach one); throwing weapons can also be thrown a few tiles, a limited number of times per match; pistols have their own magazine and range. Secondary attacks follow the shooting rules: before moving they cost 1 AP and leave a move, after moving (or after a dash) they end your turn.
  • At levels 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 your class unlocks a perk tier. Pick one of two class perks per tier in Loadout and change them between matches; some are new actions with cooldowns. The separate Perk slot works with any class.
  • Starter gear is ready at level 1; new weapons, armor, Mk upgrades and perks unlock as you level (see Loadout and Progress).
  • The storm shrinks every other round. Once the safe zone is small it stops shrinking and starts moving: the next zone is marked with a white ring (and on the minimap) two rounds ahead, then the storm slides there. When the storm closes or moves, anyone it catches gets one turn to get out before it starts hurting; anyone who was already outside keeps taking damage. Storm damage keeps rising, so keep moving with it. Supply drops are announced a round early; the pod holds the best loot in the match.
  • The strip under the top bar shows the turn order for this round, then the round break with any storm or supply event. You are highlighted, teammates are green, and enemies you cannot see show as “?”.
  • Duos: teams of two; with an odd number of humans the last one drops with an AI partner. A downed operative bleeds out in 2 turns unless an adjacent teammate revives them.
  • Trios and Quads: squads of three (up to 12 operatives on a 48×48 map) or four (up to 16 on a 56×56 map), four squads at most. Empty seats in your squad are AI squadmates. Downs and revives work as in Duos: a squad is out when nobody on it is left standing (anyone still down is eliminated with it). The storm starts wider and shrinks faster (Quads adds an early stage in round 3), there are more crates, supply drops (five in Quads) and four objectives. Unseen enemy turns play fast; the turn-order strip marks one with an amber arrow.
  • King of the Hill: teams of two on a 32×32 map with no storm. At the end of each round, a team with operatives inside the gold ring and no enemy in it scores a point (both sides inside: contested, nobody scores). The hill moves every 5 rounds; its next spot shows as a dashed ring a round ahead. First team to 8 wins; after round 24 the most points (then the most operatives standing) wins. No downs: an eliminated operative redeploys at the start of the round after next, away from enemies and the hill, with full health, ammo and utilities.
  • Siege: two teams of four, best of three rounds, sides swap after each. Defenders start inside a walled compound in the middle of the map (a door and a window in each wall, sandbags, crates) around the data core; attackers start outside under a smoke screen that clears after two rounds. Attackers win a round by holding the core (the cyan ring) with no defender in it at the end of a round, or by taking out every defender; defenders win by holding out for 10 rounds or wiping the attackers. Attackers carry 2 Breaching Charges (blow walls, doors and cover in a 1.5-tile blast clean away, 2–3 damage) and a Scout Drone; defenders trade their damaging grenades for 2 extra smoke grenades and 2 Barricades (drop a sandbag wall, half cover, on an empty ground tile within 2 tiles, not on the core). No storm, downs and revives as in Duos.
  • Rumble: teams of two in a 24×24 arena, no storm. Eliminations score for the killer’s team; first to 12 wins (or the most after round 24). Respawns as in King of the Hill.
  • Infection: everyone drops alone; at the start of round 1 one operative (two with 7 or more) turns Infected. Survivors become one team with shared sight; the Infected have claws only (dash up to 5 tiles), +2 mobility, +6 HP, regenerate 2 HP a turn and sense survivors within 10 tiles. The Infected never die: taken down, one regenerates for a turn (it can’t be hurt meanwhile) and gets back up at full HP. A survivor the Infected take out goes down “turning” and rises as Infected on its next turn. Survivors win if any of them is standing after round 15; the Infected win when nobody is left to turn.
  • Survival: co-op against waves of zombies, alone or with up to 3 more players or AI teammates (32×32 map, no storm). Zombies see only 4–6 tiles and hunt by sound: every sound shows as a ring as far as it carries. Unsuppressed gunshots carry 14 tiles, explosions 20, suppressed shots 3, melee 2, a normal move 2, a sprint (a 2-AP move) 5, doors 6 (rain shortens all of it). A zombie heads for the loudest, freshest sound it heard (yellow “?”); one that sees you chases (red “!”) and growls, pulling the others along. Walkers are the bulk; Runners are fast and fragile; closed doors hold zombies back for a couple of rounds while they bang them open, Brutes smash through doors and cover in one blow; Screamers call everything in 15 tiles to what they found; Bloaters burst into poison gas (shoot them from range, or near the horde); every 5th wave brings an Abomination. Everyone carries a Noise Maker (a beeping decoy, louder than gunfire, for 3 rounds) and a barricade. After each wave a 2-round breather brings crates, +4 HP, a barricade and fallen squadmates back. Loud noise also fills the noise meter under the minimap (explosions most, then unsuppressed fire and Noise Makers; it halves every round): a full meter sends an extra horde in from a random map edge right after the noisy turn, headed for the noise (a banner, a red edge flash and an arrow tell you where; then a 3-round rest). A noisy turn during a wave also pulls that wave's next zombies in early. Waves grow steeply (about wave² zombies), and more of them fit on the map as the waves go on. Survive 10 waves to extract; the horde difficulty is set in the waiting room.
  • Blackout: Solo at night. You see only 3.5 tiles (+1 on high ground). Anyone standing in light (a flare, near a deployed Specialist drone, in a Scout Drone’s area) or who fired an unsuppressed shot since their last turn can be seen from normal sight range. Everyone carries a flare (throw it into the dark: it lights 3 tiles until the end of next round) and crates often hold another. Every shot flashes on every minimap. Suppressed weapons and blades stay dark.
  • Mutators: in the waiting room the host (or you, offline) can switch on Low gravity, Explosive everything, One-shot, Double storm speed, Melee only and Perma-smoke for any mode. Guests see them in the room, they show as chips under the minimap in the match, and replays keep them.
  • Team pings: in Duos, Trios and Quads, tap 📍 then the map, or press and hold on the map, to ping (Enemy here, Move here, Watch this area, Loot here, Danger) or give a command (Heal me, Hold, Regroup, Push, Fall back, Revive me). Heal me calls your Medic or Engineer over to heal you (Heal Field) or restore your shield (Repair); it lights up when your HP is low, and AI teammates send it themselves when they’re hurt. Only your team sees them; they fade after 2 rounds. An AI partner or squadmates follow them (online, orders given on your own turn).
  • Specialist drone: it rides docked just above the Specialist (no vision, can’t be hit) until you tap Deploy (free, once a turn) and pick a tile. Deployed, it is its own unit with its own drone AP each turn (2; 3 with the Extended battery): fly it, zap, mark, or use its model action. Combat Protocol, Aid Protocol, Capacitor Discharge, Chain Lightning, Guardian, Haywire, Overclock, Drone Shield and Restoration all need it deployed. It sees for your team, can be shot, blown up, zapped and caught by overwatch, takes 1 storm damage a round outside the zone, and never counts as an operative (turn order, victory, objectives). Tap Drone to control it, Operative to switch back, Recall to dock it. Destroyed: Rebuild (1 AP) after 2 of your turns. Chassis: Sparrow (scout, Scan), Striker (Burst, harder zaps), Mender (Heal Pulse), Bulwark (Shield Projector, 6 HP), Jammer (Jam). Drone mastery unlocks upgrades; drone skins are in the Store.
  • Engineer: Deploy Turret (1 AP, cooldown 4) puts a sentry on an empty ground tile up to 3 tiles away: 5 HP, 3 shots, 3 rounds, sight 7. It takes one reaction shot at every enemy that moves in its sight (−15 aim like overwatch); it can be shot, blown up, zapped and jammed, and it goes down with its Engineer. Build Cover (1 AP, cooldown 2) raises half cover (6 HP) or full cover (4 HP) on a tile next to you. Repair (1 AP, cooldown 2) gives you or an ally within 3 tiles +3 shield, or a friendly turret or drone 3 HP.
  • Medic: Heal Field (1 AP, cooldown 4) marks a 1.5-tile area up to 5 tiles away; allies who start their turn in it heal 1 HP, through the end of next round. Revive Beam (1 AP, cooldown 3) revives a downed ally up to 3 tiles away in line of sight. Adrenaline (1 AP, cooldown 5): you or an ally starts its next turn with 3 AP. Passive: a Medic’s revives cost 1 AP instead of the whole turn and bring the ally back with 4 HP, and the Medic regenerates 1 HP a turn (useful in Solo too).
  • Recon: sees 2 tiles farther. Wall Scan (free, cooldown 4) reveals everything within 6 tiles, through walls, for the whole team until the end of next round. Trip Mine (1 AP, cooldown 2, two out at once) hides a mine up to 3 tiles away that only your team can see: the first enemy to step on it takes 3–4 damage, stops where it is and starts its next turn with 1 AP less. Mark Target (free, cooldown 2): your team gets +15 aim against an enemy you can see until the end of next round. In Blackout a turret sees only as far as night sight, while scans light up their area like a Scout Drone.
  • Weapon mastery: hits, damage and takedowns with a primary or sidearm level that weapon (1–10). Mastery unlocks its attachments (optic, barrel, magazine, underbarrel: picked per weapon in Loadout) and mastery finishes, up to the animated Stormcell.
  • The waiting room after Play sets up the match: add or remove bots (any size from a 1v1 up to the mode’s limit) and give each bot its own difficulty, Recruit, Veteran or Elite, or set them all at once. Difficulty changes aim, gear, memory, hearing and how cleverly they flank; an AI partner keeps gear matched to your team. Smaller matches start with a smaller storm and fewer crates, and pay less for placement.
  • Fifteen regions: Neo-Kowloon, Frostfall Station, Ember Wastes, Verdant Ruins, Ironhaven Docks, Blackwell Refinery, Sandsea Bazaar, Hollow Quarry, Mirefen Marsh, Cinder Lab, Skyreach Monastery (a gorge crossed only by rope bridges, terraces, crags and pagodas stacked three or four levels high), Underline Transit (tunnels, station platforms, parked trains and a warren of rooms full of doors), Saltglass Airfield (open salt flats and long sightlines, hangars, a control tower, little hard cover), Drowned Quarter (flooded streets, a deep canal with footbridges, a rooftop high road, junction boxes by the water) and Frostvent Caldera (a frozen lake, hot springs and geysers that erupt on a cycle). The map roulette after Deploy picks one you did not just play.
  • Play with friends: one player picks a mode, creates a lobby and shares the 5-letter code or invite link. Friends join from Play with friends and appear in the host’s waiting room, where the host adds bots and picks their difficulty. In Duos, Trios and Quads everyone picks a team and seat; bots fill the empty seats. Rooms hold up to 16 players in Quads (12 in Trios, 8 otherwise). If someone drops, AI takes over their operative.
  • Cloud save (Profile): after your first match your progress syncs to the cloud on its own (no sign-up, no email), so it survives removing the home-screen app or switching devices. Profile shows your account code: enter it with “Sign in with account code” on another device to carry on there. Without a connection everything works as before and syncs later.
  • Daily challenge: one attempt a day on the same map for everyone. Your first score of the day goes on the global leaderboard (top 50, plus your rank), shown on the results screen and in the Daily window.
  • Matches pay XP and credits. Levels unlock gear upgrades; credits and shards buy cosmetics.
  • Season pass (Pass tab): a free 45-tier track that resets every 6 weeks. Matches, the first win of the day and quest claims earn pass XP; tiers hold credits, shards, cosmetics, titles, banners and two season-exclusive items.
  • Class challenges (Profile): five goals per class, tracked in matches played as that class. They award titles (shown under your callsign) and banners (your name plate). Finish all five for the class’s prime title and banner.
